thread.title: Dow Jones, Nasdaq Creep Up; 4 Clues Apple Is Bottoming | Investor's Business Daily

author: DAVID SAITO-CHUNG
title: Dow Jones, Nasdaq Creep Up; 4 Clues Apple Is Bottoming | Investor's Business Daily
text:
The Dow Jones industrial average, Nasdaq composite and S&P 500 all showed nifty resilience in stocks today with light gains. After overcoming significant losses in the opening half-hour of trading, all three key indexes recovered lost ground to rise 0.4% to nearly 0.5% and trade at session highs with half an hour left to go.
Apple ( AAPL ), meanwhile, was causing less of a problem for all three of these indexes like the way it did during a steep drop in December. That month, the iPhone giant collapsed more than 11% following an 18% plunge the prior month. Yet on Thursday, Apple cut its loss to around 0.2%. Trading near 153, the megacap tech has now bolted nearly 8% higher from a year-to-date low of 142, set on Jan. 3.
The Nasdaq composite was off as much as 1.1% in the early going before pushing into the black. At around 6972, the tech-rich index has mirrored Apple's rebound since it too marked a 2019 low on Jan. 3.
Volume is running lower vs. the same time Wednesday on both main exchanges.
Small caps joined the rebound as well, adding another positive element to the current confirmed market uptrend. The Russell 2000 gained nearly 0.4%, making it possibly the 10th straight gain in 11 sessions.
Positive Stock Market Internals On the NYSE, winning issues led losers by a 4-3 ratio. On the Nasdaq, gainers outmatched decliners by a thinner margin of roughly 8 to 7.
Fiber optic gear firms are having a rosy 2019 so far. In IBD Leaderboard , Ciena ( CIEN ) and contract electronics specialist Fabrinet ( FN ) are hanging on to weekly gains of 6% and 13%, respectively.
Notice, on weekly charts at Investors.com and MarketSmith , how both of these stocks show superior action in the relative strength line.
Dow Jones Industrials: These Stocks Are Leading So Far In the 30-stock Dow Jones industrial average, cyclical and financial plays led the upside. Boeing ( BA ), Caterpillar ( CAT ), 3M ( MMM ) and Travelers ( TRV ) all gained 1 point or more.
Boeing, the aerospace giant, is working on a new base with a 394.38 standard buy point .
One could also view the current chart pattern as carrying the elements of a double bottom . In this case, Boeing's prime entry would be significantly lower at 369.10. In between the stock's two recent sell-offs, it hit an interim high of 369.
In a double-bottom base , add a dime to that middle peak to get a correct buy point. Also be sure to only buy stocks breaking out when the IBD current outlook is positive .
Wall Street sees Boeing growing earnings 25% last year to $15.12 a share, then raising the bottom line an additional 21% this year to $18.27 a share.
According to IBD Stock Checkup , the military and civilian passenger jet maker, which now has a joint venture with Brazil's EmbraerERJ, shows a solid Earnings Per Share Rating of 89 on a scale of 1 (terrible) to 99 (terrific).
The EPS Rating compares a company's earnings performance over the past three to five years and in recent quarters to all companies in the IBD database.
Apple And How It Can Build A Bottom One of the most powerful growth stocks since the U.S. equities market bottomed out in March 2009, Apple is definitely at a major crossroads. Shares have declined nearly 40% from a 233.47 all-time high. The stock's Accumulation/Distribution Rating is awful at a lowest possible E on a scale of A to E.
Just last week, Apple CEO Tim Cook wrote to shareholders that it's cutting quarterly revenue guidance by a shocking amount that virtually guarantees a year-over-year drop in the top line for the December-ended quarter.
So, what can IBD readers watch for to get a sense that the sellers in Apple are done, exhausted, and out?
For starters, watch for a change in the price-and-volume trends, both on a daily chart and weekly chart. Future price gains in higher volume and smaller declines in lower volume would be a big plus.
Also look at these three additional factors:
Apple retakes its fast-sliding 50-day moving average, which has trailed the speed of the stock's decline. IBD charts show the 50-day line in red. The stock makes a strong, positive reversal in price in huge volume, as seen on a weekly chart. The Nasdaq 100 component begins to showing a rising RS line , not a falling one. Even so, the stock would still need to recover more to reach any kind of acceptable entry.
Apple Profit Forecasts Today Analysts on Wall Street have recently shaved Apple's profit estimates. They expect earnings to rise just 2% to $12.17 in the current fiscal year that ends in September. But FY 2020 profit may reaccelerate to $13.53, up 11%.
From FY 2010 (ended in September that year) to FY 2018, Apple's earnings rose a cumulative 451%, from $2.16 to $11.91. That's tantamount to compounded annual growth of 25.8%.
Please read this recent IBD Stock Market Today piece on guidance for long-term Apple holders on when to consider selling and nailing down profits in the light of the stock's fourth-quarter meltdown.
Brick And Mortar Retailers Get Slammed Retailers got hit hard following a stormy update from mall-based broadline retailer Macy's ( M ). The department store giant fell more than 18% at one point, producing sympathy-style sell-offs in Kohl's ( KSS ), Ross Stores ( ROST ), Target ( TGT ) and TJX Cos .
None of these five companies show a Composite Rating of 95 or higher, according to IBD Stock Checkup . The highest belongs to TJX (91 on a scale of 1 to 99). Ross holds a decent but not great 85 score.
In the restaurants field, Wingstop ( WING ) caught its breath. The highly profitable chicken wings chain fell more than 2.6% to 69.28 in very light trading. Wingstop, a small cap with a $2 billion market value and 29 million shares outstanding, had run up almost 17% in a four-day winning streak.
Wingstop has formed a cup-style base with a 72.10 proper buy point .
In Other Financial Markets Crude oil held on to Wednesday's blistering gain of more than 5%. Near-term U.S. oil futures traded practically at break-even at $52.36 a barrel. Gold and silver eased 0.3% and 0.6%, respectively, as the U.S. dollar rebounded mildly against both the euro and the yen.
The yield on the benchmark 10-year Treasury bond edged 1 basis point lower to 2.73%.
